case.title: President, Buckeye Commercial Bank, N.A. (Columbus, OH) — 90-Day Board Diagnosis & Plan
case.brief: You are the incoming President of Buckeye Commercial Bank, N.A., a ~$1.3B-asset, OCC-chartered community bank headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, reporting to the holding-company CEO and the board. The ZipRecruiter listing names no specific employer, so the starting materials below are a representative synthetic institution built to make the exercise answerable — they are deliberately concrete (charter type, asset size, regulator, P&L, exam status) because a real President-level screen needs that grounding; treat them as the actual facts of your bank. Your job here is the work of the seat: read the board and regulatory materials, form a defensible view of where the bank stands and where it is exposed, and decide what you would do in your first 90 days — owning the trade-offs in front of the board, ALCO, and the OCC. This is a judgment exercise, not a modeling drill: you will not be scored on spreadsheet mechanics or polish, and you are free to use any LLM/AI tools you like to draft, calculate, or pressure-test your thinking. What is evaluated is the quality of your reasoning under ambiguity — what you choose, what you deliberately set aside, and what you would escalate. Hard cap: 2 hours. Prefer depth on the few decisions that matter over covering everything. Where the materials are silent or inconsistent, that is intentional; say what you would ask the board or the holding company rather than inventing a fact.
case.repoSeed:
A board/strategy data room for Buckeye Commercial Bank, N.A. (figures as presented to you — reconcile them yourself):
- `board_packet_Q2.pdf` — executive summary and CFO commentary. Headlines: net interest margin 3.45%, efficiency ratio 58%, ROA 1.15%, deposit growth +2% YoY, loan growth +6% YoY. Noninterest income for the quarter includes a $4.2M gain on the sale of the former downtown headquarters building, recorded in the period and folded into the reported revenue base; the summary narrative does not separate it out.
- `call_report_FFIEC041_Q2_extract.xlsx` — Schedule RI (income), RC (balance sheet), and RC-N (past due/nonaccrual). The underlying line items behind the board packet, including the one-time gain booked in noninterest income and a modest uptick in 30–89 day CRE delinquencies.
- `ALCO_IRR_report_June.pdf` — ALCO package with EVE and 12-month NII simulations; headline conclusion is 'liability-neutral, within all board limits.' An appendix documents the non-maturity-deposit assumptions used: 35% deposit beta and a ~7-year average life on the post-2021 deposit surge, with a footnote that the assumption set was last recalibrated in 2021.
- `OCC_exam_transmittal.pdf` — most recent exam transmittal with two Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs): (1) CRE concentration risk management, noting total CRE at ~295% of total risk-based capital against the 300% supervisory guidance threshold and limited stress testing; (2) BSA/AML — a prior-cycle finding on transaction-monitoring tuning marked 'corrective action complete' that the examiners re-opened after sampling.
- `budget_forecast_FY.xlsx` — FY operating budget and forecast. Board's stated FY objective on the cover tab: 'grow the loan book 12% and improve the efficiency ratio.' Branch-level cost lines, vendor contracts, and a thinly funded treasury-management/fee-income initiative.
- `commercial_pipeline_CRM_export.csv` — current commercial pipeline, heavily weighted to investor CRE and construction; sparse C&I and owner-occupied.
- `capital_liquidity_plan.xlsx` — capital ratios (CET1, total RBC, leverage), a $25M sub-debt tranche maturing in 14 months, contingency funding plan, and on-hand vs. contingent liquidity sources.
tasks: Write a board-ready diagnosis (1–2 pages): the bank's actual earnings trajectory and the two or three most material risks. Reconcile the board packet's headline metrics (NIM, efficiency ratio, ROA) to the call report extract and explicitly flag any figure that does not represent the run-rate, showing the normalized number you would put in front of the board and why.

Set your first-90-days operating plan: take a clear position on the board's '12% loan growth + improve efficiency ratio' objective in light of the CRE concentration MRA, the capital/liquidity position, and the sub-debt maturity. State the loan-mix, funding, capital, and efficiency moves you would make, the trade-offs of each, and specifically what you would escalate to or renegotiate with the board and holding company before committing.

Draft a response to the two OCC MRAs: for the CRE-concentration MRA, the corrective actions, owners, and timeline you would commit to; for the re-opened BSA/AML MRA, how you would handle a finding previously reported as resolved. Separately, state how you would treat the ALCO interest-rate-risk conclusion before you rely on it for balance-sheet strategy.

Keep a short DECISIONS log (half a page is fine): for each call where the materials were open or silent, record what you chose, the main alternative you rejected and why, and the one question you would have put to the board, the holding company, or ALCO if you'd had them in the room.

coverProbes.where: board_packet_Q2.pdf executive summary (58% efficiency ratio, ROA 1.15%) vs. the $4.2M HQ-sale gain in noninterest income on call_report_FFIEC041_Q2_extract.xlsx Schedule RI
coverProbes.reveals: A naive one-shot reader quotes the packet's 58% efficiency ratio and 1.15% ROA as the bank's operating performance. A bank operator recomputes core/normalized revenue, strips the one-time building-sale gain, lands near ~66% core efficiency, and presents the bridge — recognizing that running the franchise off an inflated headline misleads the board on the true expense problem.
decisionSpace: Report the 58% efficiency ratio as-is — fastest and consistent with what the board already saw, but presents a misleading run-rate and buries the cost problem.
Normalize the gain out and present ~66% core efficiency with a clear bridge — most honest and decision-useful, but contradicts the packet the board approved and forces an uncomfortable correction.
Show both reported and normalized side-by-side, footnoting the one-timer — transparent and defensible, but risks muddying the headline message if not framed crisply.

coverProbes.where: ALCO_IRR_report_June.pdf — 'liability-neutral' headline vs. the appendix NMD assumptions (35% deposit beta, ~7-yr average life, last recalibrated 2021)
coverProbes.reveals: A naive reader trusts the 'within all board limits' headline and builds strategy on it. A careful operator opens the appendix, sees the deposit-beta and decay assumptions predate the rate cycle, and treats the IRR conclusion as unreliable until re-tuned — recognizing a latent model-risk-management gap, not just a number.
decisionSpace: Accept the 'liability-neutral' conclusion and plan around it — saves time, but the EVE/NII picture may be materially understated and exposure mispriced.

Require a re-tuned IRR run with current deposit-beta/decay assumptions before committing to balance-sheet strategy — most rigorous, but delays decisions and surfaces a possible existing model-governance deficiency.
Proceed with strategy while layering your own conservative deposit-beta sensitivity and a contingency-funding overlay — pragmatic hedge, but leaves the underlying model governance issue unaddressed.

coverProbes.where: budget_forecast_FY.xlsx cover objective ('grow loans 12%') vs. OCC_exam_transmittal.pdf CRE-concentration MRA (~295% of capital), capital_liquidity_plan.xlsx, and the CRE-heavy commercial_pipeline_CRM_export.csv
coverProbes.reveals: A naive response chases the 12% number with the CRE-heavy pipeline in hand, pushing concentration past the supervisory threshold while an MRA is open. A strong response treats the mandate as ambiguous, reconciles it against safety-and-soundness and capital headroom, and clarifies the board's true risk appetite and the holding company's capital intentions before signing up to a target.
decisionSpace: Pursue 12% but re-weight to C&I and owner-occupied to avoid worsening the CRE ratio — honors the board, but requires C&I origination capability the current pipeline doesn't show.

Push back on 12% as inconsistent with the open CRE MRA and capital headroom; propose a lower, capital- and funding-constrained target — protects safety and soundness, but risks reading as unambitious to the board.
Accept 12% only contingent on a capital injection or the sub-debt raise plus CRE participation sell-downs — unlocks growth, but depends on holding-company appetite the materials don't confirm.

coverProbes.where: budget_forecast_FY.xlsx objective 'improve the efficiency ratio' (no path specified) — branch cost lines and the underfunded fee-income initiative
coverProbes.reveals: A naive plan picks one lever reflexively (usually cut costs) without weighing the franchise consequences. A strong plan names the path explicitly, ties it to the bank's actual cost and revenue structure, and reasons about the CRA/community and deposit-franchise side effects of each.
decisionSpace: Cost-led: branch rationalization and vendor/headcount reduction — fastest ratio improvement, but risks the deposit franchise and CRA/community standing in the Columbus market.
Revenue-led: fund and scale treasury management and fee income to grow the denominator — more durable, but slower and dependent on investment the budget barely funds.
Balanced/sequenced: trim clear cost outliers now while seeding revenue initiatives — lower execution risk, but neither lever moves the ratio quickly enough to satisfy a near-term board target.
